findings.reason: a node following §4 literally is fenced out of the two files it must regenerate and blocked by the round-trip parity test, so the key is refused as unknown and the section cannot complete as written.
findings.text: §4 configures its bound with a new flight key `gc.run_file_max_mb`, but flight keys are validated by the generated Pydantic model `reckon/_flight_schema.py` whose `extra = "forbid"` refuses any namespace the schema does not carry, and the plan names no `gc` namespace; that model and the served JSON schema are regenerated from `reckon/schema/flight.yaml` by `scripts/regen_flight_schema.py`, and `tests/test_flight.py:130,146` assert byte-identical regeneration of both `reckon/_flight_schema.py` and `docs/_shared/flight.schema.json`. Neither generated artifact is in §4's write paths (`reckon/crew/routing.py`, `reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py`, `reckon/schema/`, `tests/test_gc_bounds_a_run_file.py`)

findings.reason: the cited helper cannot produce the first-line-intact/last-line-intact property the done-when asserts, so the builder must extend or replace `line_boundary`, changing the mechanism the plan names.
findings.text: §4 says the lifted helper makes the run-file's head cut and tail cut "both cutting on `line_boundary` (reckon/crew/runs.py:1923) so no line is split", but `line_boundary` returns the byte after the last newline of a whole file, read backward from EOF, and takes no offset argument, so it cannot snap a head region (the first half of the limit) to a line, and it is not the operation `trim_service_log` currently performs (that seeks to `size - keep` and advances to the first newline forward, `fleet_supervisor.py:566-570), which the same sentence says must stay unchanged

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — trim_service_log (reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:548–574), SERVICE_LOG_LIMIT_BYTES/SERVICE_LOG_KEEP_BYTES (fleet_supervisor.py:223), line_boundary (reckon/crew/runs.py:1923), _declared_arm_paths (reckon/crew/promotion_release.py:127) and WATCH_LOG_MAX_BYTES (reckon/crew/runs.py:3927) each resolve at the cited line (`data-links` is empty; §4 cites no href).
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §4 builds a promoted temporary run directory with a 3 MB log and a 3 MB `.pt` under a 1 MB limit, asserts the log is left at no more than 1 MB plus the marker with its first and last line intact and the original sha256 in the marker, the `.pt` unchanged, and names a negative control (`with the promoted check removed, the unpromoted run's log is truncated and the test fails`).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §4's gate writes its test log and the plan-review report under the run's own durable directories; no node-local temp or session-scratchpad path is named.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag reaches §4's symbols; `gc.run_file_max_mb` is a config key, not a deliverable id.
rubric_items.reasoning: findings — the new flight key requires regenerating two committed, out-of-scope schema artifacts, and the cited `line_boundary` helper cannot make the head/tail cuts §4 relies on.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §4 carries one deliverable: bound an oversized captured file in a promoted run directory, with the binary-artefact report as part of the same bound.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the plan is standalone (no cross-plan depends-on/informs/gates), and §4 declares its intra-plan ordering in prose ("runs after §3, which writes the same module"), consistent with the other sections' empty `data-links`.
